title: unified-rollouts-probing-staged-shadow-autorollback-observability
author: Maya Chen
body:
Context: We want unified rollouts to support staged probing for canary + shadow flows, enabling safer progressive exposure and automated rollback based on composite metrics. This PR implements a probing controller that performs lightweight staged probes against candidate variants, integrates shadow traffic probing (for non-impactful background quality checks), and extends the autorollback engine to support multi-metric thresholds, windowed evaluation, and weighted metric aggregation. It also adds observability assets (dashboards and alerts) and e2e tests that exercise the staged-shadow-canary path.

Summary of changes: - Implement staged probing harness and scheduler (probing.py + controller integration). - Add shadow traffic balancer and sampling controls to the unified router. - Extend autorollback engine to accept composite metric policies, evaluation windows, and hysteresis to avoid flapping. - Wire metrics and tracing: new rollout metrics, per-variant probe success/failure counters, and latency/error percentiles for probing requests. - Add dashboards and alert rules for rollout health and probe regressions. - Add e2e tests and unit tests for stability guards and metric matching. - Update docs and CLI rollout tooling to expose new probe/rollback configuration.

Motivation: Canary and shadow workflows are a primary safety mechanism for model rollouts. Existing rollout behaviors allowed only simple threshold-based rollbacks and either canary or shadow when configured. Real workloads require staged probing with progressive traffic, probe-only shadow checks, and composite metric evaluation (quality + latency + resource usage). This improves safety while enabling faster rollouts for nondisruptive changes (quantization, tokenizer fixes, runtime flags).

Design highlights: - Probing controller schedules N lightweight requests (configurable) to the candidate variant in stages: dry probe, low-traffic probe, and ramped probe. Each stage emits a ProbeResult with metrics and trace id. - Shadow probing routes a sampled percentage of production requests to a candidate replica for scoring-only evaluation; these results flow into the autorollback composite metric evaluator but are marked as non-impacting to production traffic. - Autorollback now supports a Policy DSL: metrics (list), aggregation (weighted, median, max), window (seconds), and hysteresis (min stable duration before rollback). CLI and API expose defaults to keep behavior conservative. - Observability: dashboards for probe pass rates, probe latency distribution, composite metric trend with alert thresholds; tracing includes probe span tagging for correlation.

Testing and safety: - Unit tests for probe scheduler edge cases and abort paths added. - Integration tests for the router and balancer ensure no production traffic impact when shadow sampling is non-zero. - e2e test (test_staged_shadow_canary.py) simulates a degraded candidate (quality regressions + slight latency) and asserts that probing detects regression and that autorollback triggers within configured window. - Load-tested probe scheduler at 1k probes/min to validate CPU/RAM headroom; added rate-limits to avoid overload.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main and release as opt-in feature flag (rollouts.staged_probing = false by default). - Enable on internal staging and run traffic for one week. - Gradually enable for a small set of customers (dedicated staging pools) and monitor dashboards/alerts. - After 2 weeks of stable signals, flip default to enabled.

Backward compatibility: Configs without the new policy fields will continue to use existing fallback behavior (single-stage canary + simple threshold). No breaking API changes.

Documentation: Updated docs/unified-rollouts.md and CLI help text. Added examples for a composite policy that weights quality 70% and latency 30%.

Checklist: - [x] Code implements feature end-to-end - [x] Unit tests added - [x] e2e tests added - [x] Observability/dashboards added - [x] Docs updated - [x] Performance baseline validated

Impact: Small CPU increase during probe windows; measured ~3-5% additional CPU on inference fleet under typical probe schedules. Storage and metrics cardinality increased due to per-probe counters; dashboard aggregates mitigate cardinality explosion.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on autorollback aggregation logic (autorollback.py) and probe scheduler backpressure handling (probing.py). I intentionally left the default probe sample low; we can iterate on safe defaults after data from staging.

review_comments: Arjun Patel (review): Can you explain how metric weighting is normalized across different scales? Quality is 0-1 while latency is ms.
Maya Chen (reply): Added normalization step in autorollback.py and documented the approach in unified-rollouts.md; weights apply after z-score normalization. See autorollback.py lines 142-176.
Diego Ramirez (request changes): We should guard against rapid flapping if probes oscillate. Add hysteresis and min-stable-duration to the policy.
Maya Chen (reply): Hysteresis and min_stable_duration were added to the policy DSL; default 5m. Tests cover the hysteresis path.
Hannah Lee (approve): e2e looks solid and dashboards are helpful. CI green after rerun.
CI Bot: pipeline failed on first run (flake in test_probing), reran and all checks passed.
Release Manager (note): Feature gated behind rollouts.staged_probing flag; coordinate rollout with SRE on canary targets.
release_notes:
- Added staged probing controller for unified rollouts
- Added shadow traffic probing and sampling controls
- Enhanced autorollback to support composite metrics, windows, and hysteresis
- New dashboards and alert rules for rollout health
- Added e2e tests for staged-shadow-canary workflows
